subject: Arcadia - bounded p95 latency commitment request

Subject: Request: bounded p95 latency + availability commitment

Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our execs are asking for a proposal that includes both an availability target and a bounded p95 latency for inference calls (we'd like 99.95% availability and p95 <= 80ms for our typical user flows). Can Redwood provide a term sheet or addendum that outlines:

- The exact commitment (SLOs + measurement windows)
- Fallback behavior if commitments are missed
- Any capacity or dedicated reservation requirements (we're sensitive about PII and want some isolation)
- Ongoing monitoring & reporting cadence

We're aiming to close procurement by end of April — happy to share expected QPS and payload sizes if that helps. Attaching a short MLP that describes our integration pattern.

Tom
Tom Ellis
VP of Product, Arcadia Health

Team — FYI inbound from Arcadia (large health system). They want a combined availability + bounded p95 (99.95% / p95 <= 80ms). Request from procurement to see terms/addendum.

Quick asks:
- Grace: product/observability — can we formalize how we measure p95 and availability (region/ingress points)?
- Aditya: engineering — feasible to guarantee 80ms p95 for their expected workload? If not, what options (dedicated capacity, prioritized routing, reserved GPU type)?
- Laura/Stephanie: commercial — any precedent for committing bounded latency and what uplift % do we usually ask for dedicated reserved capacity?

I attached the Arcadia MLP they sent. Would like a short internal note and approval path so I can respond with a proposed addendum.

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-03-19T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: bounded p95 latency + availability commitment

Rishi / team —

Short answer: we can measure and report both metrics from the Console, but a firm external commitment requires clarifying scope and constraints. Questions to resolve before we draft an addendum:

1) Measurement windows & objectives: do they want p95 per minute, per hour, or daily aggregates? Availability window (monthly rolling)?
2) Scope: are we committing across all routes/endpoints or only for specific API keys/paths tied to their account?
3) Regions: which cloud regions will they be routed through (US-west/US-east)? Multi-region routing changes guarantees.
4) Workload profile: steady QPS vs spiky bursts will change feasible latency targets.

Suggested mitigation options we can offer:
- Redwood Dedicated with reserved GPU profile + autoscale cap for failover
- Priority routing with explicit fallback to a compatible variant (we'd need to define accepted latency delta on fallback)
- SLO credit formula (minutes of downtime or ms overage -> credit %)

I can draft the measurement/monitoring section (definition of p95 calc, synthetic checks, and reporting cadence). Need the QPS/payload info from Arcadia.

—Grace

Grace / Rishi —

From an infra/runtime perspective, 80ms p95 is aggressive but achievable with constraints. Key points:

- Platform baseline: p95 for current multi-tenant hosted instances at their average payload is ~120-150ms across US regions under normal load.
- Options to hit ~80ms p95:
  * Dedicated pool of A100/rtx-equivalent GPUs with tuned compilation and serving kernels; requires reserved capacity (monthly commitment)
  * Reduced batching window / dedicated routing for their API keys (increases per-token cost)
  * KV/prefix cache pinned for session traffic where applicable

- Capacity sizing depends on QPS and average sequence length; ask Arcadia to provide 95th percentile QPS over 1-minute windows, and the average prompt/token sizes.
- Fallback behavior: if reserved capacity exhausted, automatic fallback would route to a compatible quantized variant with higher p95 (we should set a cost/latency delta and notify client via dashboard & webhook).

Risk items to include in the addendum: warm-up latency after deploys, post-deploy performance regressions, and scheduled maintenance windows. We can accept a commitment if Arcadia purchases dedicated pool for peak capacity + a service credit model for misses.

I'll sketch an ops runbook for doing on-call escalation and capacity increase steps.

- Aditya

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: bounded p95 latency + availability commitment

Team —

Commercial playbook / negotiation notes:

- For bounded latency commitments we have historically required dedicated capacity purchases or "priority lanes" with a minimum monthly commit; typical uplift on list price is +30-60% depending on isolation and SLO tightness.
- Service credits: recommend a tiered credit schedule (small credit for single event, escalates if repeated). Legal will want explicit measurement windows and exclusion clauses for force majeure and customer-induced load.
- Approval path: goes through Sales Lead (me) -> Revenue Ops -> Legal -> CTO sign-off for infra carveouts. For anything that increases operational burden >2 FTE-months, we route through the executive exceptions committee.

I've uploaded a draft addendum (Arcadia_SLA-draft-v1.2.pdf) with suggested wording (measurement, credits, exclusion list). Please review and mark any technical caveats. Stephanie, can you run this with procurement once we have the capacity sizing?

Laura

Date: 2027-03-25T15:43:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: bounded p95 latency + availability commitment

Tom — thanks, and apologies for the multi-thread internal thread. Summary and next steps below:

Summary of the proposed path:
- Measurement: Redwood will report p95 on a rolling 1-hour window and availability on a monthly rolling window. p95 will be calculated per API key and per region; synthetic checks will run every 30s.
- Commitment (proposed): 99.95% availability monthly, p95 <= 80ms on dedicated pool (US regions) when traffic stays within the committed capacity sizing.
- Operational requirements: Arcadia to purchase a dedicated capacity pool sized to peak 95th-percentile QPS plus a 20% buffer; Redwood to reserve priority routing and implement prefix cache pinning for session flows.
- Fallback & credits: if guarantees are missed and verified (after mutually-agreed investigation) we issue service credits per the draft addendum.

Action items:
1) Tom / Arcadia: please share 1-minute granularity QPS for peak day + average sequence length, and confirm regions (US-east / US-west).
2) Aditya: draft sizing + ops runbook (ETA: 2 business days).
3) Grace: finalize monitoring definitions and dashboard feed.
4) Laura / Stephanie: commercial terms & pricing uplift to present to procurement; please prepare the addendum for legal review.

I'll attach the current draft here and kick off Legal with a signoff request once we have sizing. If you prefer, we can do a short sync this week to walk through options — proposal: 30-min call with Arcadia + Product + Infra.

Thanks everyone — I'll wait for the QPS data and then route the addendum to Legal / Exec review.

Best,
Rishi

Attachments: Arcadia_SLA-draft-v1.2.pdf, Arcadia_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx
